title: What Is White Labeling? And When It Pays in Pakistan
summary: What white labeling is, how it differs from private label, OEM and dropshipping, what a branded run really costs, and when it pays in Pakistan.
body_markdown:
White labeling means buying a product a factory already makes, then selling it under your own brand name and packaging. The product does not change. The label does.


That is the whole idea, and the catch. You are paying for a brand, not a better product, so white labeling only starts to pay once the same product is already selling for you *without* one. Brand first, find demand later, and you empty a bank account.


Which means the sequence matters more than the decision. Sell the generic version first, on stock you have not paid for —[reselling on Markaz](https://www.markaz.app/reseller-pk) runs with no minimum order and cash on delivery, so a product can prove itself before you commit cash to a branded run.


Below: what white labeling involves, how it differs from private label, OEM and dropshipping, the cost lines people forget, and the test sequence that says whether a product has earned a label.


## What white labeling actually means


A factory in China, or a manufacturer in Lahore, produces a generic item — a face serum, a power bank, a cotton kurta. It makes the same item for anyone who orders it. White labeling is the arrangement where you buy that item and the maker ships it blank, or with your artwork already applied, so you can sell it as yours.


Three things are usually yours: the brand name, the packaging, and the price. Three things usually are not: the formula or design, the production line, and the quality control. That split is why white labeling is fast to start. It is also why two sellers can be selling the identical product under different names in the same week.


Nothing about it is dishonest. It is how most supplement, cosmetics and phone-accessory brands on any marketplace began. But it does mean your brand is a promise about service, packaging and trust, not about the thing inside the box. If you cannot keep that promise better than the next seller, the label is decoration.


## White label, private label, OEM and dropshipping


These four get used as if they mean the same thing. They do not, and the difference decides how much cash you need before your first sale.


White label Private label OEM Dropshipping


**The product** Generic, sold to many sellers Made for your brand, usually exclusive Built to your own specification Someone else's, sold unbranded


**What you can change** Label and packaging Formula, finish, sizes Design, materials, tooling Nothing


**Minimum commitment** A production run A larger run Largest — often tooling too None


**Who holds the stock** You You You The supplier


**Time to first sale** Weeks Weeks to months Months Same day


Read the last two rows together. White labeling moves the stock risk onto you and asks for cash before your first branded sale. Dropshipping leaves the stock with the supplier and asks for none. Those are not competing strategies — they are different stages of the same business, and most sellers who white label successfully in Pakistan resold the same category first.


Print-on-demand sits off to one side. It brands a blank — a shirt, a mug, a phone case — one unit at a time, so you get a branded product without the run commitment. If your product can be printed rather than manufactured, start there.


## What you actually have to produce


"Just put my logo on it" turns out to be four separate jobs.


### The product itself


Pick one SKU, not a range. A brand with one proven product and a steady reorder is worth more than a brand with nine products and no repeat buyers. Order a sample before anything else and live with it for a week — shampoo, a watch strap, a kettle, whatever it is. Faults you find in week one are faults your customers would have found in week one.


### The packaging


This is where most of a first run's cost hides. A box, an inner sleeve, a seal, and an outer bag that survives a Pakistani courier network. Packaging has its own minimum too: printers quote per thousand, not per ten, which is why a small branded run can cost more per unit in packaging than in product. Our guide to[packaging and branding for small online sellers in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/packaging-branding-for-small-online-sellers-in-pakistan) covers what is worth paying for at a small scale and what is not.


### The label and the artwork


You need a name nobody else is using, a logo that still reads at thumbnail size, and label copy that is honest about what the product is. Suppliers normally want print-ready artwork in a format their printer accepts, and they will apply exactly what you send them — including the typo.


### The paperwork, where the category needs it


Some categories carry rules that have nothing to do with branding: cosmetics, food, supplements and anything electrical. Find out what your category requires in Pakistan before you print a thousand labels, not after. A brand name on a product you cannot legally sell is the most expensive kind of dead stock.


## The cost lines people forget


Ask a seller what white labeling costs and they quote the unit price. The unit price is the smallest line on the list. Roughly in order of how often they catch people out:


- **The run itself.** A branded order is a minimum order. Your cash sits in that stock until it sells, and it stops being refundable — a generic unit can go back to a supplier, a unit with your name printed on it cannot.
- **Artwork and setup.** Factories and printers often charge a one-off fee for a new design. Spread across a small run, that setup can cost more per unit than the printing does.
- **Samples, plural.** One to check the product, one to check the branded version, often a third after a correction. Each is its own shipment with its own freight.
- **Freight, duty and clearance.** If the run comes from China, landed cost is the only cost that matters, and it is never the quote. The[Alibaba alternative in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-alibaba-alternative-in-pakistan) breakdown walks through the lines that get added between a supplier's quote and your own storeroom.
- **Dead stock.** The real cost of guessing wrong. Unbranded stock that does not sell can be discounted or sent back. Branded stock that does not sell is yours permanently.


None of this makes white labeling a bad idea. It makes it a decision to take with numbers you already have, from selling the product unbranded, rather than numbers you are hoping for.


## When white labeling pays


Four conditions. The more of them you can tick honestly, the stronger the case.


### You are already reordering the same product


The strongest signal is a boring one: the same SKU sells every week and you keep restocking it. That is demand you have measured rather than assumed. Branding a product you already reorder is an upgrade. Branding a product you have never sold is a bet.


### Your customers come back


A brand only earns its cost if people buy from you twice. Consumables are the clearest case — skincare, supplements, cleaning products, anything that runs out and gets replaced. If your category is a once-in-five-years purchase, the second order you are paying for may never exist.


### The margin survives the branded unit


A branded unit costs more than a generic one: packaging, setup, the run. If your selling price cannot absorb that and still leave the margin you set, white labeling quietly converts profit into inventory. Work this out against your own real selling price before you talk to a factory, not after.


### The category rewards a brand


Some categories are bought on trust and presentation.[Cosmetics](https://www.markaz.app/shop/home-page/Cosmetics) , skincare, perfumes and baby products are the clearest examples — buyers want to know who made the thing they are putting on their skin, and a proper box changes what they will pay for it. In a category bought purely on price, it does not.


## When it does not pay


The honest version of this list is longer than the one above, and it is the one most first-time sellers need.


- **You have not sold the product unbranded yet.** The only item here that is non-negotiable. Branding captures demand; it does not create it.
- **You are competing on price.** If buyers in your category sort by lowest price and take the first result, your branded unit is simply the expensive one.
- **Your working capital is also your buffer.** A branded run locks cash in place for as long as the stock takes to sell. If that cash was also covering courier charges, returns and ad spend, one slow month turns into a crisis.
- **You want a range, not a product.** Six branded SKUs means six runs, six sets of packaging and six guesses. Nobody's first brand should be a catalogue.
- **The supplier will not send a sample.** A supplier who will not ship one unit before a branded run is a supplier whose quality you cannot check. Walk away.


## The test sequence that de-risks it


If white labeling is the destination, this is the road to it. Each step is cheap, and each one can stop you before the expensive step.


1. **Sell the generic product first.** Pick the category, list the unbranded version, and sell it on stock you have not bought. Reselling from the Markaz[shop categories](https://www.markaz.app/shop/categories) needs no minimum order and runs on cash on delivery, so this step costs effort rather than capital.
2. **Measure three things.** How often it reorders, what share of orders comes back, and what you can actually charge. Returns are the number that kills white-label plans, because once the box carries your name you inherit every one of them.
3. **Buy one unit from the source.** Before any run, get the product through the supply route you would actually use, as a single unit. The guide on how to[start China sourcing with one unit](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/no-minimum-order-start-china-sourcing-with-one-unit) sets out four ways to do that without an MOQ.
4. **Price the branded version properly.** Unit, packaging, setup, freight, duty, courier, expected returns. Compare that total against the price you proved in step two, not the price you would like to charge.
5. **Brand one SKU.** The one that earned it. Order the smallest run the supplier will accept, sell it through, and only then decide whether a second product deserves the same treatment.


Sellers who skip to step five are the ones with a room full of branded boxes. Sellers who run the sequence usually learn one of two useful things: that a product is worth branding, or that their margin was never in the brand at all — it was in picking the right product and shipping it reliably.

## Frequently asked questions


### Is white labeling legal in Pakistan?


Selling a product you bought under your own brand name is a normal commercial arrangement, provided the supplier agrees to it and your labelling is accurate. What catches people out is category rules — cosmetics, food, supplements, electrical goods — and trademark rules if the brand name is already in use. Check both before you print.


### What is the difference between white label and private label?


White label is a generic product that many sellers can put their name on. Private label is made for your brand and usually cannot be sold to your competitors. Private label buys you exclusivity and a product you can change; it costs more and commits you to a larger run.


### Do I need to register a trademark first?


You can sell without one, but you are building on sand: another seller can register the name and you would have to rebrand. If the plan is to keep the brand for years, start the registration early — and never build on a name that already belongs to someone else.


### Can I white label without importing from China?


Yes. Pakistani manufacturers white label in several categories — textiles, cosmetics, food, cleaning products — often with a smaller minimum and no freight or clearance for you to manage. For a first branded run, a local supplier you can visit usually beats a cheaper quote you cannot inspect.


### Is white labeling better than dropshipping?


It is a later stage, not a better one. Dropshipping finds out what sells with no capital at risk; white labeling captures the margin and the repeat business once you know. Doing them in the other order is how sellers lose money.


### How large should a first branded run be?


The smallest the supplier will accept, and no larger — however good the per-unit price looks at the next tier up. The point of a first run is to find out whether the branded version sells at the branded price. A volume discount is only a discount if the stock sells.
